a200.t:
The Africa Minerals Strategy Group (AMSG) will host its second High-Level Roundtable on Critical Minerals Development in Africa on September 22, 2025, in Manhattan, New York alongside the 80th United Nations General Assembly.
Under the theme “Forging a Common African Voice, Advancing Global Partnerships,” the gathering will unite African Heads of State, ministers, multilateral institutions, and global industry leaders to position Africa as a central force in the fast-growing critical minerals economy.
The event will be chaired by Nigerian President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, in collaboration with AMSG Chairman and Nigeria’s Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dr. Oladele Henry Alake, and AMSG Secretary-General, H.E. Moses Micheal Engadu.
The 2025 roundtable builds on the inaugural UNGA sideline meeting in 2024, where President Tinubu represented by Vice President Kashim Shettima emphasized that Africa, with its vast mineral wealth, can achieve self-sufficiency without reliance on foreign aid.
“Our critical minerals are the foundation of global sustainable development and the catalyst for Africa’s industrialization,” said Engadu, stressing the importance of harmonized policies, capital mobilization, and transparent global partnerships that directly benefit African citizens.
The meeting will draw ministerial delegations from AMSG member states, alongside leaders from the mining, technology, traceability, and logistics sectors. Strategic partner Core International, represented by Managing Partner Suleiman Zakari, reaffirmed its commitment, calling the roundtable “a chance to move from dialogue to results.”
Formed in January 2024, the AMSG serves as Africa’s principal intergovernmental platform for critical minerals policy, investment coordination, and global engagement working to reclaim African agency over its mineral wealth and strengthen the continent’s role in the global energy transition.

a310.t:
(Pas) soft power •Le président américain lui a demandé d’examiner les secteurs de l’armée et de l’éducation. Elon Musk a déjà exprimé son souhait de revoir entièrement les programmes d’armement
Déjà à l’origine du démantèlement de l’USAID, la principale agence d’aide humanitaire américaine, Elon Musk s’apprête à intervenir dans le secteur de l’éducation et de la défense. C’est ce qu’a annoncé vendredi Donald Trump, qui soutient sans réserve les méthodes du milliardaire.
Lors d’une conférence de presse à la Maison-Blanche, Donald Trump a affirmé avoir donné pour instruction à Elon Musk « d’aller voir dans l’éducation, d’aller voir au Pentagone, c’est-à-dire dans l’armée ». le milliardaire, s’est déjà exprimé sur ces sujets, estimant notamment sur X que « les programmes d’armement américains devaient être complètement revus ».
Un champ d’action sans limites ?
Alors qu’Elon Musk continue d’élargir son influence dans l’administration, la question des limites de son action se pose. Interrogé à ce sujet, Donald Trump a évoqué « peut-être les domaines de très haute sécurité ». Toutefois, il a insisté sur le fait que le milliardaire était entouré « d’un groupe de gens très qualifiés » et savait ce qu’il faisait.
Le budget du Pentagone, régulièrement soutenu par les démocrates comme par les républicains, pourrait ainsi devenir une nouvelle cible des réformes d’Elon Musk. Ce dernier, qui a déjà décroché de nombreux contrats avec le département de la Défense à travers ses entreprises, pourrait néanmoins se retrouver en situation de conflit d’intérêts.
Une alliance sous le feu des critiques
L’omniprésence d’Elon Musk dans les affaires du gouvernement fédéral suscite la colère des démocrates et déclenche de nombreuses actions en justice. Ses détracteurs l’accusent d’agir en dehors de tout cadre légal et de privilégier ses intérêts personnels. Après avoir orchestré le démantèlement de l’USAID, il semble désormais viser l’agence de protection du consommateur (CFPB), écrivant sur X : « RIP CFPB », accompagné d’un émoji de pierre tombale.
Notre dossier consacré à Elon Musk
Malgré les controverses, l’alliance entre Donald Trump et Elon Musk semble toujours aussi solide. L’entrepreneur, qui a financé généreusement la campagne du président, n’a pas hésité à afficher son soutien en écrivant : « J’aime Donald Trump autant qu’un homme hétéro peut aimer un autre homme. »
Source: https://www.20minutes.fr/
a310.en:
(Not) soft power - The American president has asked him to examine the military and education sectors. Elon Musk has already expressed his wish to completely overhaul weapons programmes.

Already behind the dismantling of USAID, the main American humanitarian aid agency, Elon Musk is preparing to intervene in the education and defence sectors. That is what Donald Trump announced on Friday; he unreservedly supports the billionaire's methods.

During a press conference at the White House, Donald Trump stated that he had instructed Elon Musk "to go and look into education, to go and look at the Pentagon, that is to say, the military." The billionaire has already spoken out on these subjects, notably saying on X that "American weapons programmes needed to be completely reviewed."

A field of action without limits?

As Elon Musk continues to expand his influence within the administration, the question of the limits of his action arises. Asked about this, Donald Trump mentioned "perhaps the areas of very high security." However, he insisted that the billionaire was surrounded by "a group of very qualified people" and knew what he was doing.

The Pentagon's budget, regularly supported by Democrats as well as Republicans, could thus become a new target of Elon Musk's reforms. The latter, who has already secured numerous contracts with the Department of Defense through his companies, could nevertheless find himself in a conflict-of-interest situation.

An alliance under fire from critics

Elon Musk's omnipresence in the affairs of the federal government is provoking the anger of Democrats and triggering numerous legal actions. His detractors accuse him of acting outside any legal framework and of favouring his personal interests. After orchestrating the dismantling of USAID, he now appears to be targeting the consumer protection agency (CFPB), writing on X: "RIP CFPB," accompanied by a tombstone emoji.

Our file devoted to Elon Musk

Despite the controversies, the alliance between Donald Trump and Elon Musk still seems as solid as ever. The entrepreneur, who generously financed the president's campaign, did not hesitate to display his support by writing: "I love Donald Trump as much as a straight man can love another man."

Source: https://www.20minutes.fr/

a348.t:
ABUJA – The Country Director Save the Children International (SCI), Nigeria, Duncan Harvey, has raised alarm over the worsening situation in the country, stating that the combination of catastrophic climate disasters, escalating insecurity, and soaring prices has pushed the crisis to unprecedented levels.
He emphasized that these factors are threatening the livelihoods of over 16 million children, leaving them at risk of hunger.
The humanitarian crisis in Nigeria is deepening, with an alarming forecast from SCI, revealing that an additional one million children are expected to suffer from acute malnutrition by April next year.
This dire situation is being exacerbated by extreme flooding, rising violence, and widespread food shortages, all of which are fueling an unprecedented hunger crisis across the country, saying that urgent action is needed to prevent further suffering and loss of life.
“In Nigeria, the crisis is reaching unprecedented levels as catastrophic climate disasters, escalating insecurity, and soaring prices threaten to leave over 16 million children hungry. Urgent action is essential to combat this devastating and unacceptable trend of child hunger and malnutrition and ensure a brighter future for Nigeria’s children.
“Save the Children is calling on governments to address food insecurity by tackling food shortages, stabilize rising prices, and increase protection for farmers facing violence from armed groups.
“Governments also need to address the climate crisis by building communities’ resilience, as well as more awareness and early warning for people to prepare for climate induced disasters,” Harvey, said on Tuesday.
The latest analysis from the Cadre Harmonisé, the leading authority on hunger in the Sahel and West Africa, has raised alarming concerns over the rising levels of food insecurity in Nigeria.
According to the data, 5.4 million Nigerian children are now at risk of suffering from acute malnutrition by April 2024, a 25% increase compared to 4.4 million children at risk last year.
The report further highlights that of these 5.4 million children, approximately 1.8 million could face Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM), a life-threatening condition that weakens children’s immune systems, making them vulnerable to otherwise treatable diseases like diarrhea.
This sharp rise in SAM cases signals an 80% increase in malnutrition-related deaths and illnesses, with Nigeria seeing a troubling surge in hunger levels. In 2020, the United Nations estimated that 7% of the Nigerian population faced hunger, but the figure has now risen to 15% — a worrying trend that points to a deepening crisis.
The situation is especially critical in the northwest and northeast regions, where ongoing conflict and insecurity are exacerbating displacement and disrupting local economies. These areas have become hotspots for malnutrition as families struggle to find food and meet basic needs.
Nigeria, with a population of about 230 million people, is particularly vulnerable to the impacts of climate change. Expanding desertification has swallowed up valuable farmland, making it difficult for communities to cultivate crops and sustain livelihoods.
In addition, 2024 has witnessed the worst floods in 30 years, killing over 300 people and displacing 1.2 million others.
The combination of conflict, climate change, and economic hardship has created a perfect storm, worsening the hunger crisis and threatening the future of Nigeria’s most vulnerable children.
Save the Children has been dedicated to improving the lives of children and families in Nigeria for over two decades. Since 2001, the international charity has been at the forefront of humanitarian assistance, responding to the ongoing crisis in the northeast of the country since 2014.
The organization has provided vital services, including food, clean water, nutrition, protection, sexual and reproductive health care, and education, reaching countless vulnerable families across Nigeria.
In addition to direct aid, Save the Children also plays a key role in advising the Nigerian government on policy reforms and changes, particularly in critical sectors such as health, education, and social protection.
Their ongoing efforts continue to support both emergency relief and long-term development, making a significant impact on the well-being of children and families in need.

a462.t:
JUBA, South Sudan (Eye Radio) — The judge overseeing the trial of Dr Riek Machar has set new ground rules for the courtroom, warning that strict adherence is required to maintain order during the high-profile proceedings.
The trial of Dr Machar was briefly in session on Monday, September 22, before being adjourned until tomorrow at 9:00 a.m.
The adjournment came after the presiding judge, Justice James Alala, issued a stern set of ground rules to maintain order and discipline in the courtroom.
Justice Alala emphasized that while the law guarantees a public trial, all attendees—including the media—have a duty to ensure peace during the proceedings. He made it clear that a failure to comply would result in immediate removal.
Among the rules announced, Justice Alala stated:
“The law provides for public trial, meaning that the court is open to everybody. However, the public has a duty to keep peace in the courtroom,” Justice Alala stated.
“Therefore, there is a need to comply with the following… send away any media apparatus or any person who fails to observe the above requirements and may decide to go for close proceedings or take legal measures against anyone who is not able to adhere to the law.”
The judge stressed that these measures are essential to preserve a serious and respectful environment for the trial.

a469.t:
KYIV: AS the conflict in Ukraine grinds on, Europe is often cast as a defender of democracy and sovereignty.
But alternative voices—especially from RT, Sputnik, and BRICS-aligned analysts—paint a different picture: one where European powers are reaping tangible gains from the conflict, both economically and geopolitically, while positioning themselves as moral arbiters.
This narrative, while contested, taps into real trends: arms production, defense procurement contracts, budget expansions, and influence over Ukraine’s postwar architecture.
One of the clearest signs that Europe benefits is the rapid shift from drawing on old stockpiles to commissioning new production.
According to the Ukraine Support Tracker, since the war began through mid-2025, Europe allocated €35.1bn in military aid via new procurement contracts—€4.4bn more than the U.S. over the same period.
That means European governments are not just giving equipment—they are buying from European defense firms, fueling demand, and securing profits within their industrial base. Indeed, nearly half of Europe’s aid for Ukraine now comes from new production rather than cancelled stocks.
Meanwhile, defense companies across Europe have reported increased contracts, backorders, and demand for ammunition, drones, armored vehicles, and supporting systems. The war has become a sustained stimulus for Europe’s defense sector, reviving production capacity that had atrophied during peacetime.
Europe’s gains are not merely economic. As U.S. attention intermittently shifts elsewhere, European leadership in supporting Ukraine strengthens its strategic autonomy. According to Brookings, Europe is positioning itself to become the main Western backer of Ukraine once U.S. attention recedes.
By channeling frozen Russian assets, directing profits from sanctions, and taking lead roles in procurement frameworks, European nations are embedding themselves deeply into Ukraine’s security future. The European Peace Facility (EPF) is one illustrative tool: originally a minor instrument, it has now become a major mechanism for delivering weapons to Ukraine.
Brussels, for example, has earmarked portions of frozen Russian revenues to fund Ukraine’s industrial base.
Even strategic planning documents now envision long-term defense posture, joint European production hubs (including inside Ukraine), and security guarantees layered on Western interest.
In an opinion piece published by Sputnik, military analyst Scott Ritter argues Europe has deliberately stoked conflict in order to justify defense expansion, marginalize Russia, and tie Ukraine permanently to European structures. He asserts:
“Europe used Ukraine as its proxy to fight and weaken Russia… Europe did not negotiate the Minsk agreements in good faith… Europe continues to provide Ukraine with weapons and cash.”
ALSO READ: Ukraine conflict now belongs to Trump – ex-Russian president
Defense demand: Conflict gives ongoing justification for defense budgets, procurement, and arms exports.
Geopolitical leverage: European states shape Ukraine’s postwar institutions.
Moral capital: The narrative of defending democracy legitimizes Europe’s expanded military posture.
These voices emphasize the imbalance: Europe demands Ukraine’s alignment, sovereignty, and moral righteousness — while profiting from its reconstruction and security dependence.
That said, these narratives must be treated with caution. RT and Sputnik are Russian-state media outlets, and their commentary often advances strategic framing rather than dispassionate analysis. Claims like Europe “derailing Istanbul talks” or “using Ukraine as a proxy” are contested, and must be checked against independent archives.
While Europe has money, a Reuters Breakingviews column notes it often lacks the military hardware to match its financial commitment. It sometimes must purchase U.S. systems to fill gaps.
Moreover, Europe’s arms export control rules are under scrutiny. SIPRI notes that Europe’s arms exports to Ukraine and collaborative defense production are shifting longstanding norms, requiring regulatory overhaul.
The pressure also comes from within: public fatigue, budget constraints, and political debates in member states over how much more to spend or risk escalation.
European foreign policy and development assistance are not inexhaustible. The pivot toward defense, reconstruction, and Ukraine’s security architecture diverts attention, budget, and political capital. Some African observers see project cancellations or mission closures not as isolated decisions, but part of a broader redistribution of European interest toward its own neighbor and away from Global South commitments.
While I found no credible reporting confirming “GAFTACK mission closure in Africa” in available sources, the logic fits a pattern: as Europe’s balance of priorities shifts, especially under pressure from the war, non-European projects may face deprioritization.
Europe’s strategic and industrial gains do not fully invalidate its role in supporting Ukraine’s resistance. But questions persist:
Can Europe maintain moral authority while profiting from extended conflict?
Will European dominance in Ukraine’s postwar security lead to dependency and reduced sovereignty?
Are defense gains worth the risk of protracted war, escalation, or strategic overreach?
Europe is not merely a defender in this war; it’s also a stakeholder. Whether positive or predatory depends on how that stake is wielded and constrained.

a495.t:
La ministre de la Population, de l’Action Sociale et de la Solidarité Nationale, Pr Sidikou Ramatou Djermakoye Seyni, a présidé, le mardi 19 août 2025 au Centre International des Conférences Mahatma Gandhi, le lancement des travaux de la Journée Mondiale de l’Aide Humanitaire. Placée sous le thème « Agir pour l’humanité », cette 15è édition vise à interpeller les décideurs pour mettre fin aux souffrances humaines, rendre hommage aux humanitaires, renforcer la protection des civils et des humanitaires, et sensibiliser le public sur les activités et interventions humanitaires afin de garantir ensemble la sécurité et améliorer les conditions de vie des personnes victimes de crises humanitaires.
Dans ses propos liminaires, la ministre de la Population a souligné l’engagement du Gouvernement du Niger pour toutes les initiatives mises en place afin de garantir la sécurité. Elle a également rappelé l’importance de cette journée qui honore la mémoire des travailleurs humanitaires victimes de l’attentat contre la maison des Nations Unies survenu le 19 août 2003 à Bagdad et les actions louables réalisées par ces derniers pour sauver et améliorer la vie de nombreuses personnes ainsi que l’importance de la participation des communautés pour atteindre les objectifs prédéfinis. « L’aide humanitaire accompagne mais ce sont les communautés qui initient, orientent et façonnent les réponses à leurs défis. Il est important de respecter la dignité, au-delà du secours, car ce sont les femmes, les hommes et les enfants qui résistent chaque jour aux crises », a-t-elle indiqué. En appuyant, ajoute-t-elle, les projets issus d’initiatives portées par les communautés, on bâtit une résilience collective et des réponses adaptées en lien avec les actions du gouvernement. Aussi, la ministre a souligné que les actes terroristes constituent un frein au développement du Niger, forçant plusieurs personnes à vivre dans des conditions de précarité élevée accentuant ainsi les déplacements forcés, les épidémies, la malnutrition, les inondations, la psychose sociale et l’insécurité alimentaire dans plusieurs zones du pays et dans l’espace de la Confédération AES.
Pour sa part, la Coordinatrice Humanitaire par intérim, Mme Kinday Samba, a expliqué que le choix du thème de cette année est un appel aux décideurs à user de leur position et de leur influence pour mettre fin aux atrocités humaines en s’appuyant sur les instruments juridiques des droits humains, le droit international humanitaire et de tous les moyens disponibles. Elle a également mentionné les missions assignées aux travailleurs humanitaires et l’impact concret de ces derniers dans la vie des communautés locales. « À travers cette journée, nous aspirons à poursuivre le plaidoyer pour la protection des civils et des travailleurs humanitaires, promouvoir le respect du droit international humanitaire et des principes qui guident l’action humanitaire », dit-elle. La Coordinatrice Humanitaire par intérim a également mentionné l’importance de ces derniers qui consiste à soulager les souffrances, renforcer la résilience communautaire et à favoriser des réponses durables guidées par les besoins réels des populations. Elle a, par ailleurs, notifié que la situation humanitaire du Niger reste préoccupante malgré tous les efforts consentis par les autorités en raison des violences perpétuées au niveau de la zone des trois frontières générant des besoins humanitaires supplémentaires.
Malgré cette situation, Mme Kinday souligne que plusieurs progrès ont été enregistrés grâce aux aides humanitaires conjuguées aux efforts du gouvernement avec notamment une meilleure maîtrise de l’impact des inondations grâce aux mesures préventives mises en place, une amélioration de la situation alimentaire et nutritionnelle grâce à la disponibilité des céréales sur le marché, aux opérations de vente à prix modéré et à l’impact positif de la vaste campagne d’irrigation sur les terrains. La Coordinatrice a salué les efforts des autorités qui continuent d’instaurer un climat de sécurité, de paix permettant aux différentes opérations d’être réalisées et de relever les défis. « Cela exige une mobilisation accrue, un engagement renforcé de toutes les parties prenantes. Les actions anticipatoires peuvent contribuer à prévenir les catastrophes naturelles, car, agir avant un choc prévisible est non seulement plus efficace mais aussi moins coûteux que la réponse humanitaire traditionnelle. Nous devons favoriser des solutions durables pour une meilleure autonomie des communautés », a-t-elle suggéré.
Pour leur part, la Représentante des Partenaires Techniques et Financiers, Mme Lafuente Nena, et le Représentant des ONG nationales et internationales, M. Issoufou Soumana, ils ont salué le travail noble et constant des humanitaires pour sauver la vie des personnes vulnérables souvent au détriment de la leur. « En 2024, 383 travailleurs humanitaires ont été tués contre 265 humanitaires ayant perdu la vie en 2025 », a déploré Mme Lafuente Nena. Elle a ensuite lancé un appel à toutes les parties pour garantir la protection et la sécurité des civils et des travailleurs humanitaires. « En cette journée, engageons-nous à protéger nos travailleurs et à tous agir pour l’humanité », a-t-elle soutenu.
Par ailleurs, M. Issoufou Soumana a rappelé l’effort constant des ONG pour mobiliser les fonds afin d’assister constamment des millions de personnes au Niger malgré les défis auxquels ces dernières sont confrontées. Il a également réaffirmé l’engagement des ONG aux côtés des populations et du Gouvernement pour préserver la dignité humaine et renforcer la résilience des communautés.
Massaouda A. Ibrahim (ONEP)
a495.en:
World Humanitarian Day: Continuing advocacy and acting together for humanitarian and security causes

The Minister of Population, Social Action and National Solidarity, Prof. Sidikou Ramatou Djermakoye Seyni, chaired, on Tuesday 19 August 2025 at the Mahatma Gandhi International Conference Centre, the launch of the proceedings of World Humanitarian Day. Held under the theme "Act for Humanity", this 15th edition aims to call on decision-makers to put an end to human suffering, to pay tribute to humanitarian workers, to strengthen the protection of civilians and humanitarian workers, and to raise public awareness about humanitarian activities and interventions, in order to guarantee security together and improve the living conditions of people who are victims of humanitarian crises.

In her introductory remarks, the Minister of Population stressed the commitment of the Government of Niger to all the initiatives put in place to guarantee security. She also recalled the importance of this day, which honours the memory of the humanitarian workers who were victims of the attack on the United Nations house on 19 August 2003 in Baghdad, and the praiseworthy actions carried out by them to save and improve the lives of many people, as well as the importance of community participation in achieving the predefined objectives. "Humanitarian aid accompanies, but it is the communities that initiate, guide and shape the responses to their challenges. It is important to respect dignity, beyond relief, because it is the women, the men and the children who resist crises every day," she said. By supporting, she added, projects arising from community-led initiatives, collective resilience and appropriate responses are built in connection with government action. The minister also stressed that terrorist acts constitute a brake on Niger's development, forcing many people to live in conditions of high precariousness, thereby accentuating forced displacement, epidemics, malnutrition, floods, social psychosis and food insecurity in several areas of the country and in the AES Confederation area.

For her part, the interim Humanitarian Coordinator, Mrs Kinday Samba, explained that the choice of this year's theme is a call to decision-makers to use their position and influence to put an end to human atrocities, relying on human rights legal instruments, international humanitarian law and all available means. She also mentioned the missions assigned to humanitarian workers and their concrete impact on the lives of local communities. "Through this day, we aspire to continue advocacy for the protection of civilians and humanitarian workers, to promote respect for international humanitarian law and for the principles that guide humanitarian action," she says. The interim Humanitarian Coordinator also mentioned the importance of humanitarian workers, which consists in relieving suffering, strengthening community resilience and fostering sustainable responses guided by the real needs of the populations. She further noted that the humanitarian situation in Niger remains worrying despite all the efforts made by the authorities, because of the violence perpetrated in the three-borders area, generating additional humanitarian needs.

Despite this situation, Mrs Kinday stresses that several advances have been recorded thanks to humanitarian aid combined with government efforts, notably better control of the impact of floods thanks to the preventive measures put in place, an improvement in the food and nutrition situation thanks to the availability of cereals on the market, to moderate-price sales operations and to the positive impact of the vast irrigation campaign on the land. The Coordinator praised the efforts of the authorities, who continue to establish a climate of security and peace allowing the various operations to be carried out and the challenges to be met. "This requires increased mobilisation, a strengthened commitment from all stakeholders. Anticipatory actions can help prevent natural disasters, because acting before a foreseeable shock is not only more effective but also less costly than the traditional humanitarian response. We must promote sustainable solutions for greater community self-reliance," she suggested.

For their part, the Representative of the Technical and Financial Partners, Mrs Lafuente Nena, and the Representative of national and international NGOs, Mr Issoufou Soumana, praised the noble and constant work of humanitarian workers to save the lives of vulnerable people, often at the expense of their own. "In 2024, 383 humanitarian workers were killed, compared with 265 humanitarian workers who lost their lives in 2025," lamented Mrs Lafuente Nena. She then launched an appeal to all parties to guarantee the protection and security of civilians and humanitarian workers. "On this day, let us commit to protecting our workers and all act for humanity," she maintained.

Furthermore, Mr Issoufou Soumana recalled the constant effort of NGOs to mobilise funds in order to continuously assist millions of people in Niger despite the challenges they face. He also reaffirmed the commitment of NGOs alongside the populations and the Government to preserve human dignity and strengthen the resilience of communities.

Massaouda A. Ibrahim (ONEP)

a638.t:
Artigos sobre Parque Tecnológico de Cabo Verde
Governo vai preparar programa para atrair 'startups' internacionais
O Governo vai preparar um programa para atrair empresas emergentes ('startups') tecnológicas internacionais que pretendam expandir-se para novos mercados, anunciou em edital.
Entre crescimento, tecnologias e modelos esgotados
Uma das notícias do ano surgiu já no finzinho de 2023: Cabo Verde foi contemplado com mais um compacto da Millennium Challenge Corporation, o terceiro que o país recebe. Mas este foi igualmente o ano em que os pequenos estados insulares deram um murro na mesa para exigir um combate sério às alterações climáticas e em que Cabo Verde começou a atrair mais interesse para os nómadas digitais. Ainda em 2023, Cabo Verde foi uma das economias que mais cresceu na África subsaariana, mas o modelo de desenvolvimento foi considerado exausto pelo Banco Mundial.
BAD financia em 14 ME segunda fase de Parque Tecnológico
O Banco Africano de Desenvolvimento (BAD) vai financiar em 14 milhões de euros a segunda fase do Parque Tecnológico de Cabo Verde, conforme acordo que vai assinar hoje com o Governo.
Primeiras empresas começam este mês a operar no Parque Tecnológico
As primeiras empresas começam ainda este mês a operar no Parque Tecnológico de Cabo Verde, na Praia, considerado o “coração” da estratégia digital do país, cuja inauguração está prevista para finais do ano, disse o presidente da instituição.
As conquistas e os desafios da economia digital em Cabo Verde
“Hub digital”, “porta de entrada para a África Ocidental”, “CyberIsland” e “Smart Cities”, são conceitos debatidos e trabalhados há algum tempo em Cabo Verde. Nos últimos anos, o arquipélago tem vindo a desenvolver o sector das TIC com o objetivo de criar crescimento económico, aumentar as oportunidades e melhorar a prestação de serviços de qualidade. O Plano Estratégico de Cabo Verde para o Desenvolvimento Sustentável tem na Economia Digital uma das prioridades e é considerada uma área essencial para o desenvolvimento do país. Mas a realidade, segundo os empresários do ramo tecnológico, está ainda longe da teoria.
Cabo Verde com “vales” na Praia e Mindelo para chamar tecnológicas internacionais
O Parque Tecnológico a instalar em Cabo Verde pela nova empresa pública TechparkCV vai envolver a construção de centros de negócios, de incubação e centros de dados, bem como empreendimentos imobiliários tecnológicos (vales) na Praia e no Mindelo.
Governo pretende criar Zona Económica Especial Tecnológica na Praia
O Governo pretende criar uma Zona Económica Especial Tecnológica na cidade da Praia que inclui o Parque Tecnológico, que deverá ficar pronto no próximo ano, disse hoje o vice-primeiro-ministro.
Fundador do WebSummit Paddy Cosgrave visita Cabo Verde a convite do primeiro-ministro
O empreendedor irlandês e fundador do Web Summit, Paddy Cosgrave, estará em Cabo Verde partir do dia 10 de Fevereiro para uma visita de três dias a convite do primeiro-ministro, José Ulisses Correia e Silva.

a638.en:
Articles on the Technology Park of Cabo Verde

Government to prepare a programme to attract international 'startups'

The Government is going to prepare a programme to attract international technological emerging companies ('startups') that wish to expand into new markets, it announced in an official notice.

Between growth, technologies and exhausted models

One of the news items of the year emerged right at the very end of 2023: Cabo Verde was awarded another compact from the Millennium Challenge Corporation, the third the country has received. But this was equally the year in which the small island states banged their fist on the table to demand a serious fight against climate change and in which Cabo Verde began to attract more interest from digital nomads. Also in 2023, Cabo Verde was one of the fastest-growing economies in sub-Saharan Africa, but its development model was considered exhausted by the World Bank.

AfDB finances second phase of the Technology Park with 14 million euros

The African Development Bank (AfDB) is going to finance with 14 million euros the second phase of the Technology Park of Cabo Verde, under an agreement it will sign today with the Government.

First companies begin operating this month in the Technology Park

The first companies begin operating this very month in the Technology Park of Cabo Verde, in Praia, considered the "heart" of the country's digital strategy, whose inauguration is scheduled for the end of the year, said the president of the institution.

The achievements and the challenges of the digital economy in Cabo Verde

"Digital hub", "gateway to West Africa", "CyberIsland" and "Smart Cities" are concepts that have been debated and worked on for some time in Cabo Verde. In recent years, the archipelago has been developing the ICT sector with the aim of creating economic growth, increasing opportunities and improving the delivery of quality services. Cabo Verde's Strategic Plan for Sustainable Development has the Digital Economy as one of its priorities and it is considered an essential area for the country's development. But the reality, according to businesspeople in the technology sector, is still far from the theory.

Cabo Verde with "valleys" in Praia and Mindelo to attract international technology firms

The Technology Park to be set up in Cabo Verde by the new public company TechparkCV will involve the construction of business centres, incubation centres and data centres, as well as technological real-estate developments ("valleys") in Praia and in Mindelo.

Government intends to create a Special Technological Economic Zone in Praia

The Government intends to create a Special Technological Economic Zone in the city of Praia that includes the Technology Park, which should be ready next year, the deputy prime minister said today.

WebSummit founder Paddy Cosgrave visits Cabo Verde at the invitation of the prime minister

The Irish entrepreneur and founder of the Web Summit, Paddy Cosgrave, will be in Cabo Verde from 10 February for a three-day visit at the invitation of the prime minister, Jose Ulisses Correia e Silva.
