By Jones Gadama
The papacy, a position steeped in tradition and history, has long been characterized by the practice of newly elected popes adopting the names of their predecessors. This custom, while rich in significance, raises important questions about identity, continuity, and the evolving nature of the Catholic Church.
As we stand on the brink of a new papal election, it is time to consider the merits of a pope embracing his own name rather than adopting the moniker of an ancient pontiff.
This argument is not merely a matter of personal preference; it is a call for authenticity, a reflection of the contemporary world, and an opportunity to redefine the papacy for future generations.
First and foremost, the act of choosing a name is deeply personal and symbolic.
A pope’s name carries weight and meaning, often reflecting the values, aspirations, and vision of the individual who holds the office. By adopting a name that resonates with his own identity, the incoming pope can establish a unique connection with the faithful, fostering a sense of authenticity and relatability.
In an age where transparency and personal connection are increasingly valued, a pope who chooses his own name can signal a departure from the past and a commitment to addressing the challenges of the present.
Moreover, the Catholic Church is at a crossroads, facing numerous contemporary issues that require fresh perspectives and innovative solutions.
The world is changing rapidly, and the Church must adapt to remain relevant. By choosing a name that reflects his own vision and mission, the new pope can signal a willingness to engage with the complexities of modern life.
This could include addressing pressing issues such as climate change, social justice, and the role of technology in society. A name that embodies these concerns can serve as a rallying point for the faithful, inspiring them to take action and engage with the world around them.
Tradition, while important, should not be an unyielding constraint. The Catholic Church has a rich history of adaptation and reform, and the choice of a papal name should be viewed through this lens. The Church has evolved over the centuries, responding to the needs of its followers and the challenges of the times.
Embracing a new name can be seen as a continuation of this tradition of evolution, allowing the Church to remain dynamic and responsive to the needs of its congregation. The next pope has the opportunity to honor the past while also paving the way for a more inclusive and forward-thinking Church.
Furthermore, the practice of adopting a name from the past can inadvertently create a sense of distance between the pope and the people. When a pope chooses a name that is steeped in history, it can evoke a sense of nostalgia but may also alienate those who feel disconnected from that history.
A name that resonates with contemporary issues and values can foster a sense of belonging and inclusivity among the faithful. It can serve as a reminder that the Church is not merely a relic of the past but a living institution that is engaged with the present and future.
In addition, the choice of a name can have significant implications for the pope’s legacy. A name that reflects the pope’s own identity and vision can shape how he is remembered in history.
By choosing a name that embodies his mission and values, the incoming pope can leave a lasting impact on the Church and the world. This legacy can inspire future generations of Catholics to engage with their faith in meaningful ways, fostering a sense of continuity and purpose.
The argument for a new name is also supported by the notion of personal accountability. A pope who chooses his own name is taking ownership of his role and responsibilities.
It signifies a commitment to leading the Church with integrity and authenticity, rather than merely following in the footsteps of those who came before him. This sense of accountability can resonate with the faithful, who are increasingly seeking leaders who are willing to take risks and challenge the status quo.
Moreover, the Catholic Church is a global institution, with followers from diverse cultural backgrounds and experiences. A pope who chooses a name that reflects his own identity can help to bridge cultural divides and foster a sense of unity among the faithful.
This is particularly important in a world that is often marked by division and conflict. A name that resonates with a broader audience can serve as a powerful symbol of inclusivity and solidarity, reminding Catholics that they are part of a global community.
The choice of a name also has implications for the Church’s relationship with other faiths and denominations. In an increasingly pluralistic world, a pope who embraces his own identity can foster dialogue and understanding among different religious traditions.
By choosing a name that reflects his own values and beliefs, the incoming pope can signal a commitment to interfaith engagement and collaboration. This can help to build bridges between communities and promote a spirit of cooperation in addressing shared challenges.
Furthermore, the act of choosing a name can serve as a powerful statement of hope and renewal. The Catholic Church has faced numerous challenges in recent years, from scandals to declining attendance.
A pope who chooses his own name can embody a spirit of renewal and transformation, signaling a commitment to addressing these challenges head-on. This can inspire the faithful to engage with their faith in new and meaningful ways, fostering a sense of hope for the future.
The tradition of adopting a papal name is a significant aspect of the papacy, but it should not be an unyielding constraint.
The incoming pope has a unique opportunity to embrace his own identity and choose a name that reflects his vision, values, and commitment to the Church and the world.
By doing so, he can foster a sense of authenticity, inclusivity, and accountability, while also signaling a willingness to engage with the complexities of modern life. The choice of a name is not merely a matter of tradition; it is a powerful statement of identity and purpose.
As the Catholic Church continues to navigate the challenges of the 21st century, a new name can serve as a beacon of hope and renewal, inspiring the faithful to engage with their faith in meaningful ways.
It is time for the next pope to step into the future with a name that is uniquely his own, embracing the rich tapestry of the Church’s history while also charting a new course for the future
Pope Francis’ funeral to be held on Saturday as world leaders pay tribute
By Jones Gadama
The Vatican has announced that the funeral of Pope Francis will be held on Saturday, April 26, at 10:00 am local time in St. Peter’s Square, with world leaders including US President Donald Trump and Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelensky expected to attend.
Pope Francis, the Argentine pontiff who led the Catholic Church for over a decade, passed away on Monday, April 21, at the age of 88 due to complications from a stroke.
The funeral service, which will be presided over by the dean of the College of Cardinals, Cardinal Giovanni Battista Re, is expected to draw huge crowds to the Vatican.
After the Mass, Pope Francis’ coffin will be taken inside St. Peter’s Basilica and then to the Rome basilica of Santa Maria Maggiore for burial, as per his wishes expressed before his death.
In a departure from tradition, Pope Francis had requested a simpler funeral, eschewing the traditional pomp and ceremony.
He had also specified that he wanted to be buried in the Santa Maria Maggiore basilica, not in St. Peter’s Basilica, saying “The Vatican is the home of my last service, not my eternal home”.
The Pope’s coffin was displayed in St. Peter’s Basilica on Tuesday, allowing the faithful to pay their respects.
The funeral Mass will include prayers on behalf of the people of Rome, because the pope was their bishop, and on behalf of Eastern-rite Catholics.
The Gospel reading will be from St. John’s account of Jesus asking Peter, “Do you love me?” and telling him, “Feed my sheep”.
Pope Francis’ death has sparked an outpouring of tributes from around the world, with leaders from various countries and faiths paying their respects.
Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Guo Jiakun expressed condolences on behalf of China, highlighting Pope Francis’ efforts to improve relations between China and the Vatican.
Pope Francis, born Jorge Mario Bergoglio, was known for his humility and commitment to serving the poor.
During his papacy, he championed various causes, including climate action, social justice, and interfaith dialogue.
His passing marks the end of an era for the Catholic Church, and his legacy will be remembered for generations to come.
The funeral rites, as revised by Pope Francis himself, emphasize the hope and witness to the faith that those baptized in Christ “will rise with him to new life”.
The ceremony will include a procession, the funeral Mass, and burial, with the Pope’s body being placed in a zinc-lined wooden coffin.
A metal tube containing a copy of the “rogito”, a legal document attesting to the Pope’s death and burial, will be buried with him.
The Pope’s death has sparked tributes from around the world, with leaders and ordinary people alike paying their respects.
In the Philippines, hundreds gathered for a mass at the Manila Cathedral to bid goodbye to the late pope, remembering his outreach to the poor and survivors of natural disasters.
As the world comes together to pay tribute to Pope Francis, his funeral on Saturday will be a celebration of his life, legacy, and commitment to serving others.
The ceremony will be a testament to the impact he had on the lives of millions, and his message of hope and compassion will continue to inspire people of all faiths and backgrounds.

a4836.t:
Segundo as constatações da avaliação, o sistema de Prontidão e Resposta a Emergências de Cabo Verde encontrava-se, no final de 2019, nas etapas iniciais de desenvolvimento, apresentando uma pontuação global baixa quando comparado com padrões internacionais. Muitos elementos fundamentais simplesmente não estavam em vigor, o que levou os avaliadores a classificarem o sistema como estruturalmente frágil e altamente vulnerável a perdas humanas, sociais e económicas em caso de catástrofe.
Entre os aspectos mais críticos identificados, destaca-se a ausência de um Sistema de Gestão de Informações eficaz, elemento-chave para coordenar acções de emergência. Sem esse mecanismo, não é possível integrar dados de diferentes instituições, o que limita a capacidade de resposta rápida e coordenada. A inexistência de planos de evacuação em massa para ilhas como o Fogo (onde apenas existe plano para Chã das Caldeiras) e Santo Antão foi igualmente considerada alarmante, dado o risco real de erupções vulcânicas e outros desastres naturais. Já a Brava, que também era mencionada no relatório, dispunha à época de um plano de evacuação.
O diagnóstico revelou ainda a falta de abrigos e de espaços preparados para acolher populações deslocadas, bem como a debilidade das infra-estruturas de resposta de emergência. No campo da formação, a avaliação concluiu que os municípios carecem de serviços de protecção civil devidamente estruturados, com recursos humanos qualificados e equipamentos adequados, deixando as comunidades mais expostas e sem meios básicos para lidar com crises.
Apesar das fragilidades, o relatório reconhece avanços importantes, sobretudo no enquadramento legal e institucional. Cabo Verde dispõe de legislação básica na área da protecção civil, incluindo a Lei de Bases da Protecção Civil (2012) e o Plano Nacional de Contingência (2010), embora muitos dos dispositivos previstos ainda não tenham sido implementados. A pontuação mais elevada do diagnóstico foi precisamente no critério da responsabilidade legislativa, ainda que considerada insuficiente face às necessidades práticas do país.
Incêndios e Resgate
Outro ponto positivo foi identificado no combate a incêndios urbanos e no resgate técnico, onde bombeiros voluntários e profissionais têm desempenhado um papel relevante. Contudo, a avaliação alertou para a falta de critérios claros de selecção e de normas sobre requisitos mínimos de pessoal e de equipamentos, o que compromete a eficácia das corporações. Em alguns casos, bombeiros no activo não cumprem os padrões físicos necessários para responder a situações extremas.
Coordenação de apoio
A análise sublinhou ainda a ausência de coordenação internacional estruturada para apoio em emergências, uma lacuna grave para um pequeno Estado insular exposto a riscos múltiplos. Embora Cabo Verde tenha acesso a mecanismos de cooperação, como os da União Europeia, a falta de protocolos internos e de mecanismos de articulação clara faz com que a ajuda externa não seja mobilizada de forma eficiente.
Os autores do diagnóstico apontam que, em termos de envolvimento comunitário, existem boas práticas pontuais, lideradas por organizações como a Cruz Vermelha de Cabo Verde, mas que estas iniciativas não são suficientes para criar uma cultura nacional de prontidão. A educação das comunidades, a realização de simulacros e a capacitação de líderes locais são áreas praticamente ausentes ou ainda em fase incipiente.
Em termos de recomendações, o relatório defende um reforço urgente do sistema de Prontidão e Resposta a Emergências, com prioridade para a criação de um sistema nacional de gestão de informação integrado, o desenvolvimento de planos de evacuação inter-ilhas e a definição de normas claras para os serviços municipais de protecção civil. É igualmente enfatizada a necessidade de investir na formação contínua de profissionais, de aumentar a coordenação entre os níveis nacional e municipal e de envolver mais activamente a sociedade civil e o sector privado.
O diagnóstico conclui que, embora Cabo Verde já tenha lançado as bases legais e políticas para a protecção civil e a gestão de riscos, a distância entre o quadro jurídico e a realidade operacional é ainda grande. Para os especialistas, transformar estratégias em acções concretas será fundamental para reduzir a vulnerabilidade do país e proteger os ganhos de desenvolvimento alcançados nas últimas décadas.
Texto originalmente publicado na edição impressa do Expresso das Ilhas nº 1240 de 3 de Setembro de 2025.
a4836.en:
According to the findings of the assessment, Cabo Verde's Emergency Preparedness and Response system was, at the end of 2019, in the early stages of development, showing a low overall score when compared with international standards. Many fundamental elements were simply not in place, which led the assessors to classify the system as structurally fragile and highly vulnerable to human, social and economic losses in the event of a disaster.

Among the most critical aspects identified, the absence of an effective Information Management System stands out, a key element for coordinating emergency actions. Without that mechanism, it is not possible to integrate data from different institutions, which limits the capacity for a rapid and coordinated response. The non-existence of mass evacuation plans for islands such as Fogo (where a plan exists only for Cha das Caldeiras) and Santo Antao was likewise considered alarming, given the real risk of volcanic eruptions and other natural disasters. Brava, which was also mentioned in the report, did at that time have an evacuation plan.

The diagnosis further revealed the lack of shelters and of spaces prepared to receive displaced populations, as well as the weakness of emergency response infrastructure. In the field of training, the assessment concluded that the municipalities lack properly structured civil protection services, with qualified human resources and adequate equipment, leaving communities more exposed and without basic means to deal with crises.

Despite the weaknesses, the report acknowledges important advances, above all in the legal and institutional framework. Cabo Verde has basic legislation in the area of civil protection, including the Civil Protection Framework Law (2012) and the National Contingency Plan (2010), although many of the provisions foreseen have still not been implemented. The highest score in the diagnosis was precisely in the criterion of legislative responsibility, even if considered insufficient in view of the country's practical needs.

Fires and Rescue

Another positive point was identified in fighting urban fires and in technical rescue, where volunteer and professional firefighters have played a relevant role. However, the assessment warned of the lack of clear selection criteria and of standards on minimum staffing and equipment requirements, which undermines the effectiveness of the fire brigades. In some cases, serving firefighters do not meet the physical standards needed to respond to extreme situations.

Coordination of support

The analysis further underlined the absence of structured international coordination for support in emergencies, a serious gap for a small island state exposed to multiple risks. Although Cabo Verde has access to cooperation mechanisms, such as those of the European Union, the lack of internal protocols and of clear coordination mechanisms means that external aid is not mobilised efficiently.

The authors of the diagnosis point out that, in terms of community involvement, there are isolated good practices, led by organisations such as the Cabo Verde Red Cross, but that these initiatives are not sufficient to create a national culture of preparedness. The education of communities, the holding of drills and the training of local leaders are areas that are practically absent or still at an incipient stage.

In terms of recommendations, the report argues for an urgent strengthening of the Emergency Preparedness and Response system, with priority for the creation of an integrated national information management system, the development of inter-island evacuation plans and the definition of clear standards for municipal civil protection services. Equally emphasised is the need to invest in the continuous training of professionals, to increase coordination between the national and municipal levels and to involve civil society and the private sector more actively.

The diagnosis concludes that, although Cabo Verde has already laid the legal and policy foundations for civil protection and risk management, the distance between the legal framework and operational reality is still great. For the specialists, turning strategies into concrete actions will be fundamental to reducing the country's vulnerability and protecting the development gains achieved in recent decades.

Text originally published in the print edition of Expresso das Ilhas no. 1240 of 3 September 2025.

a4934.t:
Dar es Salaam. Ripoti ya uagizaji wa bidhaa kutoka nje kwa mwaka 2024 inaonyesha uagizaji mkubwa wa vifaa vya viwandani, hali inayoakisi ukuaji wa sekta ya viwanda nchini.
Takwimu zinaonyesha kuwa jumla ya Sh43.076 trilioni zilitumika kuagiza bidhaa mbalimbali, huku vifaa vya viwandani vikiongoza kwa thamani ya Sh11 trilioni, ikifuatiwa na chuma na bidhaa zake (Sh7.02 trilioni).
Wachumi wameeleza kuwa ongezeko hili linahusiana moja kwa moja na juhudi za Serikali kukuza uchumi wa viwanda kupitia miradi ya maendeleo na sera za uwekezaji.
Kwa mujibu wa ripoti hiyo, sekta ya viwanda imekuwa mhimili muhimu wa maendeleo ya uchumi, hali inayosababisha mahitaji makubwa ya mitambo, mashine na vifaa vingine vya viwandani.
Mhadhiri wa uchumi wa Chuo cha elimu ya biashara (CBE), Dk Dickson Pastory alisema: “Kutokana na mazingira mazuri yaliyowekwa na Serikali, yamevutia wawekezaji kutoka nje, hivyo kuongezeka kwa wawekezaji viwandani kumesababisha kuongezeka kwa uagizaji wa vifaa vya viwandani.”
Alisema miongoni mwa mambo yaliyosisimua sekta ya uzalishaji nchini ni kubadilishwa kwa sera ya uwekezaji ambako kumechangia baadhi ya viwanda kuondolewa kodi na tozo kwa ajili ya kuongeza uwekezaji.
Mchambuzi mwingine wa uchumi, Dk Thobiasi Swai, alisema: “Kwa ujumla inaonekana viwanda vimeongezeka nchini, hivyo kuongezeka kwa uagizaji wa bidhaa ni lazima ili kuwezesha uzalishaji wa bidhaa viwandani.”
Naye mhadhiri wa Chuo Kikuu cha Kikatoliki Mbeya, Balozi Morwa alionya juu ya athari zitokanazo na ongezeko hili, akisema kuna haja ya vifaa hivyo kuzalishwa nchini ili kupunguza matumizi makubwa ya fedha za kigeni.
“Kuongezeka kwa uagizaji kunaonesha kuwa hatuna uzalishaji wa vifaa vya viwandani, ni muhimu kufikiria mbinu za kujenga uwezo wa kuzalisha vifaa hivi ndani ya nchi. Hii itasaidia kupunguza matumizi ya fedha za kigeni na kuimarisha uchumi wa ndani zaidi," alisema.
Aidha, ongezeko la mahitaji ya vifaa vya viwanda huenda lina uhusiano mkubwa na ongezeko la uwekezaji nchini, kwani, Januari 10, 2024, Mkurugenzi wa Kituo cha Uwekezaji Tanzania (TIC), Gilead Teri katika kipindi cha Januari hadi Desemba 2024, Kituo cha Uwekezaji Tanzania (TIC) kilisajili jumla ya miradi 901, ukilinganisha na miradi 526 iliyosajiliwa katika kipindi kama hicho mwaka 2023.
Kwa mujibu wa Teri, miradi hii imeweza kuvutia mtaji wa Sh23.5 trilioni ukilinganisha na mtaji Sh14.44 trilioni iliyotokana na miradi ya uwekezaji kupitia TIC katika kipindi cha Januari hadi Disemba 2023.
Mikoa mitano inayoongoza kwa kusajili miradi ya uwekezaji nchini ni Dar es Salaam (356), Pwani (166), Arusha (64), na Dodoma (47), ambapo asilimia 70.3 (miradi 633) ilisajiliwa katika mikoa hii.
Sekta tano zinazoongoza kwa kusajili miradi mingi ya uwekezaji ni uzalishaji viwandani (miradi 377, 41.8%), usafirishaji (miradi 138, 15.3%), ujenzi wa majengo ya biashara (miradi 91, 10.1%), utalii (miradi 76, 8.4%) na kilimo (66, 7.3%).
a4934.en:
Dar es Salaam. The report on imports of goods from abroad for the year 2024 shows large imports of industrial equipment, a situation that reflects the growth of the country's industrial sector.

The statistics show that a total of 43.076 trillion shillings was spent on importing various goods, with industrial equipment leading at a value of 11 trillion shillings, followed by iron and its products (7.02 trillion shillings).

Economists have explained that this increase is directly related to the Government's efforts to grow the industrial economy through development projects and investment policies.

According to the report, the industrial sector has become an important pillar of economic development, a situation that creates a large demand for plant, machinery and other industrial equipment.

A lecturer in economics at the College of Business Education (CBE), Dr Dickson Pastory, said: "Because of the good environment put in place by the Government, foreign investors have been attracted, so the increase in industrial investors has led to an increase in the importation of industrial equipment."

He said that among the things that have stimulated the country's manufacturing sector is the change in investment policy, which has contributed to some industries being exempted from taxes and levies in order to increase investment.

Another economic analyst, Dr Thobiasi Swai, said: "On the whole it appears that industries have increased in the country, so an increase in the importation of goods is inevitable in order to enable the production of manufactured goods."

For his part, a lecturer at Mbeya Catholic University, Balozi Morwa, warned about the effects arising from this increase, saying there is a need for such equipment to be produced domestically in order to reduce the heavy use of foreign currency.

"The increase in imports shows that we have no production of industrial equipment; it is important to think of ways of building the capacity to produce this equipment within the country. This will help reduce the use of foreign currency and strengthen the domestic economy further," he said.

Furthermore, the increase in demand for industrial equipment may well be closely related to the increase in investment in the country, because, on January 10, 2024, the Director of the Tanzania Investment Centre (TIC), Gilead Teri, [said that] in the period from January to December 2024 the Tanzania Investment Centre (TIC) registered a total of 901 projects, compared with 526 projects registered in the same period in 2023.

According to Teri, these projects were able to attract capital of 23.5 trillion shillings, compared with capital of 14.44 trillion shillings from investment projects through TIC in the period from January to December 2023.

The five leading regions for registering investment projects in the country are Dar es Salaam (356), Pwani (166), Arusha (64), and Dodoma (47), where 70.3 percent (633 projects) were registered.

The five leading sectors for registering the most investment projects are manufacturing (377 projects, 41.8%), transport (138 projects, 15.3%), construction of commercial buildings (91 projects, 10.1%), tourism (76 projects, 8.4%) and agriculture (66, 7.3%).

a5057.t:
Vor 50 Jahren
1975-01-07
            
                        
                
            CLEMENS KAPUUO SCHLÄGT GEGEN SWAPO ZURÜCK 
Windhoek – In einer langen Stellungnahme weist Hererochef Clemens Kapuuo die gegen ihn und die Nationale Konvention gerichteten Angriffe durch SWAPO scharf zurück. Clemens Kapuuo ist gleichzeitig steilvertretender Vorsitzender der Nationalen Konvention. Er wurde in der letzten Zeit von SWAPO heftig attackiert. Seine jüngste Antwort, die abschriftlich an den Generalsekretär der Vereinten Nationen, den sogenannten UNO-Kommissar für Namibia, die Botschafter der Vereinigten Staaten und Englands sowie an die Bundesregierung in Bonn ging, hat folgenden Wortlaut:
„Südwestafrika ist ein Land, das sich noch unter kolonialer Herrschaft befindet. Die Kolonisierung Südwestafrikas, die noch bis zum heutigen Tage besteht, begann durch Deutschland. Zu Beginn des 20, Jahrhunderts, als Deutschland Truppen nach Südwestafrika sandte, fand ein bitterer Krieg zwischen den Deutschen und den afrikanischen Stämmen in Südwestafrika statt. Der Krieg wurde in den zentralen und südlichen Teilen Südwestafrikas ausgetragen. Die Afrikaner wurden mit großer Brutalität unterdrückt. Unter dem infamen Ausrottungsbefehl der deutschen Administration unter Herrn von Trotha sollten alle Männer, Frauen und Kinder getötet werden. Als Ergebnis des Ausrottungsbefehls wurde mehr als die Hälfte des gesamten Hererostammes vernichtet.
APPELL AN DIE ARBEITER
Ondangwa – Der Chefminister von Owambo Filemon Elifas richtete heute einen Appell an das Ovambovolk, in dem er auf die Bedeutung der Wahlen verwies. In Owambo findet vom 13. bis 17. Januar eine Wahl zum Gesetzgebenden Rat statt. Die gewählten Abgeordneten werden nach der Wahl gegenüber den traditionellen Führern in der Mehrheit sein, Chefminister Elifas richtete in seiner Ansprache auch einen Appell an die Arbeitgeber außerhalb von Owambo, den wahlberechtigten Ovambos die Möglichkeit zur Stimmabgabe zu geben. In ganz Südwestafrika sind Wahllokale eingerichtet. Ein besonderer Appell geht an die Farmer, ihre Farmarbeiter zum nächsten Wahllokal zu bringen.
Während SWAPO in Owambo selbst nach außen hin nicht stark in Erscheinung tritt, bemüht sich die Organisation, wenigstens im Süden den Wahlboykott zu propagieren. SWAPO hat es bekanntlich abgelehnt, Kandidaten aufzustellen. SWAPO argumentiert, dass in ganz Südwestafrika eine Wahl nach dem Grundsatz ein Mann eine Stimme stattfinden müsse und nicht in einzelnen ethnischen Gebieten.
Chefminister Filemon Elifas betonte dagegen die Eigenständigkeit von Owambo und ruft alle Ovambos auf, von ihrem Stimmrecht Gebrauch zu machen. Die Arbeitgeber bittet er um entsprechende Hilfe.
UMTRIEBE DER „HARE-KRISCHNA“-JÜNGER
Frankfurt / Pinneberg – Auf dem Frankfurter Polizeipräsidium sind – zwei Wochen nach der spektakulären Polizeiaktion gegen die sogenannte „Hare Krishna“-Sekte erneut 29 Anhänger dieser religiösen Gemeinschaft gelandet. Die kahlgeschorenen Krishna-Jünger mit ihren gelben Gewändern, die im Schloss Rettershof im Taunus ihre Hauptquartiere haben, waren am Abend des zweiten Weihnachtstages vor der Frankfurter Haftanstalt Preungesheim aufgetaucht, um ihrem dort in Untersuchungshaft sitzenden „Tempelpräsidenten" Peter Kaufmann (24) und seinem Stellvertreter Stefan Kess (27) rhythmische Gesänge darzubringen.
Wie ein Polizeisprecher berichtete, kamen die singenden „Mönche“ – darunter acht Frauen – zwar nach einer Stunde der Aufforderung der Polizei nach, sich zu zerstreuen. Als sie mit ihren drei Kleinbussen dann allerdings in Richtung Polizeipräsidium fuhren, wurden sie in der Innenstadt von der Polizei gestoppt und zur Überprüfung ihrer Personalien ins Präsidium gebracht. Ihnen wird Verstoß gegen das Versammlungsgesetz vorgeworfen.
MISSERFOLG DER GOLDAUKTION
Washington – Die große amerikanische Goldauktion ist ein Misserfolg, indem die Amerikaner es verschmähten, die Chancen zum Kauf des wertvollen Metalls auszunutzen. Trotz der ungewissen wirtschaftlichen Lage und einer Inflationsrate von zwölf Prozent mieden es die Amerikaner, an der graten Goldauktion in der Geschichte teilzunehmen. Ihre Haltung führte dazu, dass am Montagnachmittag in den Börsenschluss-Stunden der Goldpreis auf 167 Dollar je Unze zurückfiel, nachdem der Preis am Jahresende beinahe die 200-Dollar-Grenze überschritten hatte.
Das amerikanische Finanzministerium brachte am Montag zwei Millionen Unzen Gold zur Auktion. Das Schatzamt hat aIle Angebote mit einem Preis von über 153 Dollars je Unze angenommen, d. h. etwa 20 Dollars unter dem Preis in London. Dies ist eine der Hauptursachen, warum der Goldpreis weiter zurückfiel. Die Absicht der amerikanischen Regierung, mit der Auktion den Goldpreis zu dampfen, ist damit erfüllt worden.
ANGOLA-KONFERENZAM 10. JANUAR
Lissabon – Der Minister für die Überseeterritorien, Antonio de Almeida Santos, erklärte der Agentur Reuter, der Erfolg der Angola-Konferenz hänge mehr von der Zusammenarbeit der drei angolanischen Truppen, als vom guten Willen der portugiesischen Regierung ab. Es könne kein Zweifel über die Absichten und über die Unparteilichkeit der portugiesischen Regierung bestehen, nach einer uneigennützigen Lösung für Angola zu suchen.
Es ist noch nicht bekannt, wo am 10. Januar die Konferenz zwischen den drei angolanischen Gruppen und der portugiesischen Regierung eröffnet wird. Man nimmt an, dass sie irgendwo in der Provinz Algarve im südlichen Portugal stattfindet.
Windhoek – In einer langen Stellungnahme weist Hererochef Clemens Kapuuo die gegen ihn und die Nationale Konvention gerichteten Angriffe durch SWAPO scharf zurück. Clemens Kapuuo ist gleichzeitig steilvertretender Vorsitzender der Nationalen Konvention. Er wurde in der letzten Zeit von SWAPO heftig attackiert. Seine jüngste Antwort, die abschriftlich an den Generalsekretär der Vereinten Nationen, den sogenannten UNO-Kommissar für Namibia, die Botschafter der Vereinigten Staaten und Englands sowie an die Bundesregierung in Bonn ging, hat folgenden Wortlaut:
„Südwestafrika ist ein Land, das sich noch unter kolonialer Herrschaft befindet. Die Kolonisierung Südwestafrikas, die noch bis zum heutigen Tage besteht, begann durch Deutschland. Zu Beginn des 20, Jahrhunderts, als Deutschland Truppen nach Südwestafrika sandte, fand ein bitterer Krieg zwischen den Deutschen und den afrikanischen Stämmen in Südwestafrika statt. Der Krieg wurde in den zentralen und südlichen Teilen Südwestafrikas ausgetragen. Die Afrikaner wurden mit großer Brutalität unterdrückt. Unter dem infamen Ausrottungsbefehl der deutschen Administration unter Herrn von Trotha sollten alle Männer, Frauen und Kinder getötet werden. Als Ergebnis des Ausrottungsbefehls wurde mehr als die Hälfte des gesamten Hererostammes vernichtet.
APPELL AN DIE ARBEITER
Ondangwa – Der Chefminister von Owambo Filemon Elifas richtete heute einen Appell an das Ovambovolk, in dem er auf die Bedeutung der Wahlen verwies. In Owambo findet vom 13. bis 17. Januar eine Wahl zum Gesetzgebenden Rat statt. Die gewählten Abgeordneten werden nach der Wahl gegenüber den traditionellen Führern in der Mehrheit sein, Chefminister Elifas richtete in seiner Ansprache auch einen Appell an die Arbeitgeber außerhalb von Owambo, den wahlberechtigten Ovambos die Möglichkeit zur Stimmabgabe zu geben. In ganz Südwestafrika sind Wahllokale eingerichtet. Ein besonderer Appell geht an die Farmer, ihre Farmarbeiter zum nächsten Wahllokal zu bringen.
Während SWAPO in Owambo selbst nach außen hin nicht stark in Erscheinung tritt, bemüht sich die Organisation, wenigstens im Süden den Wahlboykott zu propagieren. SWAPO hat es bekanntlich abgelehnt, Kandidaten aufzustellen. SWAPO argumentiert, dass in ganz Südwestafrika eine Wahl nach dem Grundsatz ein Mann eine Stimme stattfinden müsse und nicht in einzelnen ethnischen Gebieten.
Chefminister Filemon Elifas betonte dagegen die Eigenständigkeit von Owambo und ruft alle Ovambos auf, von ihrem Stimmrecht Gebrauch zu machen. Die Arbeitgeber bittet er um entsprechende Hilfe.
UMTRIEBE DER „HARE-KRISCHNA“-JÜNGER
Frankfurt / Pinneberg – Auf dem Frankfurter Polizeipräsidium sind – zwei Wochen nach der spektakulären Polizeiaktion gegen die sogenannte „Hare Krishna“-Sekte erneut 29 Anhänger dieser religiösen Gemeinschaft gelandet. Die kahlgeschorenen Krishna-Jünger mit ihren gelben Gewändern, die im Schloss Rettershof im Taunus ihre Hauptquartiere haben, waren am Abend des zweiten Weihnachtstages vor der Frankfurter Haftanstalt Preungesheim aufgetaucht, um ihrem dort in Untersuchungshaft sitzenden „Tempelpräsidenten" Peter Kaufmann (24) und seinem Stellvertreter Stefan Kess (27) rhythmische Gesänge darzubringen.
Wie ein Polizeisprecher berichtete, kamen die singenden „Mönche“ – darunter acht Frauen – zwar nach einer Stunde der Aufforderung der Polizei nach, sich zu zerstreuen. Als sie mit ihren drei Kleinbussen dann allerdings in Richtung Polizeipräsidium fuhren, wurden sie in der Innenstadt von der Polizei gestoppt und zur Überprüfung ihrer Personalien ins Präsidium gebracht. Ihnen wird Verstoß gegen das Versammlungsgesetz vorgeworfen.

Washington – Die große amerikanische Goldauktion ist ein Misserfolg, indem die Amerikaner es verschmähten, die Chancen zum Kauf des wertvollen Metalls auszunutzen. Trotz der ungewissen wirtschaftlichen Lage und einer Inflationsrate von zwölf Prozent mieden es die Amerikaner, an der graten Goldauktion in der Geschichte teilzunehmen. Ihre Haltung führte dazu, dass am Montagnachmittag in den Börsenschluss-Stunden der Goldpreis auf 167 Dollar je Unze zurückfiel, nachdem der Preis am Jahresende beinahe die 200-Dollar-Grenze überschritten hatte.

Fifty Years Ago
1975-01-07

CLEMENS KAPUUO HITS BACK AT SWAPO
Windhoek – In a long statement, Herero chief Clemens Kapuuo sharply rejects the attacks directed against him and the National Convention by SWAPO. Clemens Kapuuo is at the same time deputy chairman of the National Convention. He has recently been fiercely attacked by SWAPO. His latest reply, copies of which were sent to the Secretary-General of the United Nations, the so-called UN Commissioner for Namibia, the ambassadors of the United States and England, as well as to the Federal Government in Bonn, reads as follows:
“South West Africa is a country that is still under colonial rule. The colonisation of South West Africa, which continues to this day, began with Germany. At the beginning of the 20th century, when Germany sent troops to South West Africa, a bitter war took place between the Germans and the African tribes in South West Africa. The war was fought in the central and southern parts of South West Africa. The Africans were suppressed with great brutality. Under the infamous extermination order of the German administration under Mr von Trotha, all men, women and children were to be killed. As a result of the extermination order, more than half of the entire Herero tribe was wiped out.”

APPEAL TO THE WORKERS
Ondangwa – The Chief Minister of Owambo, Filemon Elifas, today issued an appeal to the Ovambo people in which he pointed to the importance of the elections. In Owambo, an election to the Legislative Council takes place from 13 to 17 January. After the election, the elected representatives will be in the majority over the traditional leaders. In his address, Chief Minister Elifas also appealed to employers outside Owambo to give Ovambos entitled to vote the opportunity to cast their ballots. Polling stations have been set up throughout South West Africa. A special appeal goes out to the farmers to bring their farm workers to the nearest polling station.
While SWAPO does not appear strongly in public in Owambo itself, the organisation is endeavouring, at least in the south, to propagate a boycott of the election. SWAPO has, as is known, refused to put forward candidates. SWAPO argues that an election must be held throughout South West Africa on the principle of one man, one vote, and not in individual ethnic areas.
Chief Minister Filemon Elifas, by contrast, emphasised the autonomy of Owambo and calls on all Ovambos to make use of their right to vote. He asks employers for corresponding assistance.

ACTIVITIES OF THE “HARE KRISHNA” DISCIPLES
Frankfurt / Pinneberg – At Frankfurt police headquarters, two weeks after the spectacular police operation against the so-called “Hare Krishna” sect, 29 followers of this religious community have once again ended up. The shaven-headed Krishna disciples in their yellow robes, who have their headquarters at Rettershof Castle in the Taunus, had turned up on the evening of the second day of Christmas in front of the Frankfurt Preungesheim detention centre in order to offer rhythmic chants to their “temple president” Peter Kaufmann (24) and his deputy Stefan Kess (27), who are being held there in pre-trial detention.
As a police spokesman reported, the singing “monks” – among them eight women – did comply after an hour with the police's request to disperse. However, when they then drove with their three minibuses in the direction of police headquarters, they were stopped by the police in the city centre and taken to headquarters for a check of their personal details. They are accused of violating the Assembly Act.

FAILURE OF THE GOLD AUCTION
Washington – The great American gold auction is a failure, in that the Americans spurned the opportunity to buy the valuable metal. Despite the uncertain economic situation and an inflation rate of twelve percent, Americans avoided taking part in the largest gold auction in history. Their attitude meant that on Monday afternoon, in the closing hours of trading, the gold price fell back to 167 dollars per ounce, after the price had almost crossed the 200-dollar mark at the end of the year.
The American Treasury put two million ounces of gold up for auction on Monday. The Treasury accepted all bids at a price above 153 dollars per ounce, i.e. about 20 dollars below the price in London. This is one of the main reasons why the gold price fell further. The American government's intention of dampening the gold price by means of the auction has thereby been fulfilled.

ANGOLA CONFERENCE ON 10 JANUARY
Lisbon – The Minister for the Overseas Territories, Antonio de Almeida Santos, told the Reuters agency that the success of the Angola conference depends more on the cooperation of the three Angolan forces than on the goodwill of the Portuguese government. There can be no doubt about the intentions and the impartiality of the Portuguese government in seeking a selfless solution for Angola.
It is not yet known where the conference between the three Angolan groups and the Portuguese government will open on 10 January. It is assumed that it will take place somewhere in the province of the Algarve in southern Portugal.

a5135.t:
President John Dramani Mahama has officially launched the long-anticipated 24-hour economy and accelerated export development programme, dubbed the 24-hour Agenda, describing it as a national reset and a bold step toward self-reliance, inclusivity and prosperity.
Delivering the keynote address at the launch ceremony in Accra on July 2, 2025 the President declared: “The path is going to be challenging, but we will succeed. And we will succeed with discipline, coordination and shared purpose.”
He described the agenda as the beginning of a new model of economic development, one grounded in productivity, powered by the private sector and coordinated by the state.
Tracing the roots of the 24-hour Agenda, President Mahama explained that the vision was inspired by deep reflection during and after his previous administration.
He described Ghana’s economic model as one trapped in a cycle of unequal exchange exporting raw materials and importing finished goods a system that enriches foreign economies while leaving Ghanaian youth unemployed and industries stagnant.
“We ship cocoa, gold, timber and oil abroad, only to repurchase them as chocolates, jewelry, furniture and fuel at a far greater cost. This model does not serve our people. It generates foreign jobs and funds foreign healthcare and education systems,” he stated.
The 24-hour economy concept, which once resonated as a mere slogan, during the 2020 and 2024 election seasons, has now evolved into what he calls a “coherent, integrated and multi-sectoral national strategy.”
The 24 hour Pillars
President Mahama was quick to emphasize that the 24-hour Agenda is not merely about working longer hours, but about unleashing productivity, expanding opportunity and boosting exports.
At the heart of the agenda are eight synergistic sub-programme, each with a specific focus:
GROW24: Enhancing agricultural productivity, food security and agro-processing
MAKE24: Revitalising manufacturing and industrialisation
PAGE24: Accelerating construction, housing and public infrastructure
SHOW24: Developing creative, cultural and tourism assets
CONNECT24: Fixing logistics, warehousing, energy and digital infrastructure
FUND24: Unlocking innovative financing through credit guarantees, blended finance and venture capital
ASPIRE24: Building a skilled, ethical and digitally savvy workforce
GO24: Engaging all sectors religious, civic, security and academic in national productivity and pride
“These are not just names. They represent a structural rethinking of how we target job-rich, export-oriented sectors and build forward and backward linkages across the economy,” the President explained.
One of the most ambitious features of the programme is the Border Economic Corridor, a flagship intervention aimed at unlocking the economic and environmental potential of Ghana’s inland regions and reconnecting with Sahelian neighbors.
He announced that, “We will recreate over 2 million hectares of high-intensity agriculture under GROW24. We will establish agro-industrial parks for textiles, pharmaceuticals, and food processing, and tourism clusters along the lake under SHOW24.
“We will turn the lake into a central transport highway that connects north to south, east to west under CONNECT24.”
He painted a vivid picture of a transformed Ghana: fresh produce from Tamale air-freighted daily to Europe, vibrant aquaculture sustaining jobs, and modern logistics infrastructure slashing transport costs by up to 80%.
This, he said, was the realisation of Kwame Nkrumah’s dream of an integrated economic corridor powered by Akosombo, long overdue for revival.
Addressing how the programme will be funded, Mahama emphasized that the government’s role will be catalytic, not dominant.
“Government will facilitate, not control. Enterprise financing will come from commercial banks, development finance institutions, and blended instruments. Government funds will be used primarily for bulk infrastructure and to support a soon-to-be-autonomous 24-hour Plus Authority.”
He announced that FUND24 will be tasked with addressing capital access issues, providing credit guarantees, and avoiding breach of Ghana’s fiscal responsibilities to international lenders.
The authority, currently under a presidential secretariat, will evolve into a permanent institution that reports directly to the President, not just him, but “the next President and the next after that.”
In concluding his address, President Mahama issued a call to national duty, inviting labour unions, the private sector, traditional leaders, youth groups, civil society, and development partners to fully embrace the 24hour agenda.
“This programme is for Ghana’s future. It is a national strategy to ensure inclusive growth, export expansion, job creation, and structural transformation. Ghana belongs to all of us. The work of transformation must be the task of all of us.”

a5297.t:
The authorities in Nampula this week began the construction of resilient homes to rehouse 69 families from Mossuril affected by Cyclone Jude, which hit the province and northern Mozambique generally in March, it was announced today.
“At the moment, around 16 houses are under construction. It is a gradual process that involves not only the craftsmen, but also the population itself, who are being trained in this construction process. But in total, 69 houses will be built,” said the administrator of the Mossuril district, Alfredo Maxlhaieie.
The situation at stake is that of 69 households resettled in the Moanona II neighbourhood, in Mossuril district, 174 km from the provincial capital, Nampula, who saw their homes, farmland and schools destroyed by the cyclone on March 10. They are currently receiving humanitarian assistance.
In view of the consequences of the successive cyclones that have affected northern Mozambique in recent years, the aim is to build cyclone-resilient houses, valued at around 120,000 meticais (€1,630) each.
Mozambique is considered one of the world geographies most severely affected by global climate change, experiencing cyclical floods and tropical cyclones during the rainy season, as well as prolonged periods of severe drought.
According to Maxlhaieie, Cyclone Jude affected more than 200,000 people in Mossuril, corresponding to 26,000 families who continue to receive assistance from various partners in their areas of residence, “both in terms of food supplies, agriculture and water supply”.
Cyclone Jude, the most recent to affect the country, made landfall in Mozambique via the district of Mossuril, causing at least 43 deaths, 41 of them in Nampula, but also affecting Tete, Manica and Zambézia in the centre of the country, and Niassa and Cabo Delgado in the north.
In the last rainy season, which runs from October to April, Mozambique was also hit by Cyclones Chido on 14 December and Dikeledi on 13 January, leaving a trail of deaths and destruction. During this period, at least 313 deaths were attributed to the cyclones, and 1.9 million people were otherwise affected by the storms.

#La Russie a remis plus de 350 tonnes d'huile de tournesol au Niger

a5425.en:
#Russia has delivered more than 350 tonnes of sunflower oil to Niger
#Russia has delivered more than 350 tonnes of sunflower oil to Niger
On 26 March, the ceremony for the handover of Russian humanitarian aid took place in Niamey with the participation of the Ambassador of the Russian Federation to Niger and Mali, Igor Gromyko, the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced on 1 April.
The delivery was organised jointly with the World Food Programme #UN.
According to the WFP, the Russian aid will make it possible to supply the most vulnerable, including refugees, for three months.

a5466.t:
The Minister of Education, Professor Tahir Mamman, recently directed the West African Examinations Council (WAEC) and the National Examinations Council (NECO), both institutions that conduct the Senior School Certificate Examinations (SSCE), to reject applicants who are less than 18 years of age. It would be the second time that the professor of law would set tongues wagging about age requirements for higher education in Nigeria. In his earlier attempt to enforce it, Mamman had instructed the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) to ensure only students who were 18 years and above sat for the University Tertiary Matriculation Examinations (UTME) for admission into Nigerian universities in 2024, but he backed down after his instruction was opposed by stakeholders.
As it were, the minister is not introducing a new policy. Attaining the age of 18 had always been a requirement for sitting for SSCE, except that over the years this age requirement was observed in the breach, with the introduction of the creche, playgroup, and other pre-primary stages into the education system, especially in privately-owned institutions. It created the opportunity for parents to take two-year-old children to playgroups that are turned into formal learning environments to hasten their transition into primary school at a very tender age. Parents have little or no time to bond with these children, and, therefore, fail to teach family and community values to them. Rather, young children are compelled to read, write, and engage in intellectual exercises at a time, psychologically, they should only enjoy the love and care of parents, play games, learn to sing rhymes, and appreciate the beauty of the world around them.
The Ministry of Education’s Quality Assurance department has ignored this trend and even permitted the promotion of young children into junior secondary schools from Primary 4 or Primary 5. The majority of students admitted into junior secondary schools rarely completed the six-year requirement for primary school leaving certificates. It is acceptable that exceptional pupils or geniuses or pupils with a high intelligent quotient could be given accelerated promotion, but that should be an exception, not the norm, as practiced in schools. Today, both the weak and brilliant students skip Primary 6.
Nigerians are living with the consequences of rushing children through the primary and secondary education system, as the objectives of primary and secondary education are hardly achieved. In his authoritative work, the Nigerian Education System, C.O. Taiwo articulates the objectives of primary education to include: “the development of sound standards of individual conduct and behaviour; an understanding of the community and of what is of value for its development, and of the contribution which the individual can make to the community; the development of a lively curiosity leading to a desire for knowledge about the immediate environment and the world outside; permanent literacy; and the acquisition of some skill of hand and a recognition of the value of manual work.”
- NIGERIA DAILY: How Victims Of Flooding Struggle To Get Back On Their Feet
- Nigerian Exporters Hub appoints Mr. Babatunde Faleke as new Managing Director
Pupils who pass through our primary schools hardly achieve a half of the above objectives. They struggle with the basic skills of reading and writing, not to talk of basic handicraft. In Nigeria, many graduates of secondary schools hardly acquire the skills for employment or self-employment, enumerated in the 6-3-3-4 system. Many ‘brilliant’ students who rush out of secondary schools at the age of 14, 15 or 16 hardly acquire the skills of woodwork/carpentry; electrical installation; livestock farming; fine arts, food and nutrition, which should make them independent.
In many developed societies, the average age for students’ admission into tertiary institutions is 18, though those who demonstrate exceptional brilliance are admitted at a younger age.
We support the federal government’s move to ensure that students mature socially and psychologically upon completion of secondary education and, probably attain the age of 18. However, preventing those, who due to the lapses in the implementation of age policy, from sitting for SSCE may be inimical to their progress. Asking them to remain at home for, say, one or two years before sitting for the SSCE could affect their performance in those examinations.
In order not to put students at a disadvantage, government must implement this policy in primary and secondary schools simultaneously, by insisting that no child is admitted into Primary 1 if he or she is less than six years. Primary 6 classes should be mandatory for all primary school pupils. This way, only children who are 12 years of age could enter into junior secondary schools, to complete secondary education at 18. But for the Nigerian secondary education, age qualification for writing SSCE is not a major issue. The government has the challenge of investing heavily in the achievement of the diversity contained in the curriculum of Secondary Education, as that is the only way of effectively preparing young Nigerians for the future.

a5478.t:
The United States Embassy in Juba said it is working with humanitarian partners – through the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) – to help address the ongoing cholera outbreak in South Sudan.
In a press statement, the U.S. Embassy said it is providing funding to UN agencies and medical charity MSF to deliver emergency water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) services and provide life-saving medical care.
Other priority measures include supporting vaccination campaigns, provision of treatment kits and diagnostic tests, and raising public awareness to curb the spread of cholera.
On December 29, USAID said it delivered more than 2 million Aquatab water purification tablets as part of the humanitarian response to the ongoing cholera outbreak.
The tablets, it said, will treat six million gallons of water, providing safe drinking water to communities most affected by the outbreak.
In addition to these efforts, the United States has committed $200,000 to the World Health Organization (WHO) to support cholera response activities in South Sudan.
“This funding will enhance public awareness campaigns on the dangers of cholera and prevention measures such as safe water use, proper food handling, and good hygiene practices,” the embassy said.
“It will also strengthen WASH interventions and equip health officials with critical resources to treat cases effectively.”
Since cholera was confirmed in Upper Nile State on October 23, the outbreak has spread rapidly, with more than 13,206 cases and 199 deaths reported as of December 29.
The Aquatabs donation and additional funding underscore the United States’ steadfast commitment to supporting the people of South Sudan.
The diplomatic mission reaffirmed Washington’s support to the South Sudanese people “during this challenging time”, adding that the assistance will save lives and help prevent the spread of cholera in vulnerable communities.
“We renew our call on South Sudan’s transitional government to start using public revenue to address its people’s health needs, provide other basic services, and to pay public sector salaries for health workers, other civil servants, and security personnel.”
